sections.heading: Who pays after a Royal Oak crash

c.v: Your own auto insurer pays these benefits regardless of fault (MCL 500.3107):

items.v: your medical expenses, up to the PIP level you chose
85 percent of lost wages for up to three years, up to the monthly cap DIFS sets each year
replacement services at $20 a day
attendant care

c.v: If you have no policy, a resident relative’s policy pays (MCL 500.3114). If none exists, an occupant claims from the insurer of the vehicle they were in (MCL 500.3114(4)), and then the Michigan Assigned Claims Plan (MCL 500.3172), capped at $250,000 for medical benefits. A pedestrian or cyclist hit by a car, with no household policy, claims through the Assigned Claims Plan (MCL 500.3115)

The insurer must receive written notice within one year (MCL 500.3145(1)). It must pay each bill within 30 days of reasonable proof, or owe 12 percent interest (MCL 500.3142). Since the 2019 reform, PIP medical coverage is no longer unlimited unless you chose it, so the level on your declarations page matters. See our
Your claim against the at-fault driver.

For pain and suffering, you need a threshold injury: death, serious impairment of body function, or permanent serious disfigurement (MCL 500.3135(1)). A serious impairment is an objectively manifested impairment of an important body function that affects your general ability to lead your normal life. It does not have to be permanent (MCL 500.3135(5);
You can also recover economic losses that no-fault does not cover (MCL 500.3135(3)(c)):

items.v: lost wages beyond the three years or above the monthly cap
medical bills above your chosen PIP level

c.v: The suit must be filed within three years (MCL 600.5805(2)). The mini tort claim recovers up to $3,000 in vehicle damage not covered by your policy (MCL 500.3135(3)(e)). If the at-fault driver’s insurer will not pay it, the claim is filed in the 44th District Court.
Drunk drivers and the dram shop claim.

A bar, restaurant, or store that serves a visibly intoxicated person, or a minor, is liable for the injuries that person causes under Michigan’s dram shop act (MCL 436.1801). For a crash after a night downtown, the bar’s commercial policy is often larger than the drunk driver’s auto policy. The claim has its own rules:

items.v: Written notice must go to the business within 120 days after you hire a lawyer.
The drunk driver must be named and kept in the suit.
The suit must be filed within two years, not three (MCL 436.1801(3), (4)).

“Visibly intoxicated” has to be shown by what the server could see, so the evidence matters: point-of-sale records, the bar’s cameras, ride-share and parking records, and witnesses who saw the driver served.

c.v: That evidence is overwritten or forgotten within weeks. See our

faqs.question: A driver pulled out of a Woodward turnaround and hit me. Who is at fault?

answer.v: Usually the driver leaving the turnaround, who must yield to traffic on Woodward. These crashes are often disputed, though. The turnaround’s signal or sign, the sight lines, and your speed all matter. Photograph the turnaround and get the witnesses. Woodward belongs to MDOT.

faqs.question: The driver who hit me had just left a bar downtown. Can I sue the bar?

answer.v: Possibly. A bar that served a visibly intoxicated person can be liable for the injuries that person causes. Written notice is due within 120 days after you hire a lawyer, and suit within two years. The bar’s sales records and cameras are the evidence, and they disappear quickly.

faqs.question: I was hit crossing Main Street at night. Who pays my medical bills?

answer.v: Your own household’s auto policy pays first. If you have none, the Assigned Claims Plan pays. (MCL 500.3115.) Your pain-and-suffering claim is against the driver, reduced by any share of fault the evidence assigns you. That is why the signal phase and the downtown cameras matter.
